_comment: Raptor's egg library (library/README.md). Written for Raptor.
name: Etherpad
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: Etherpad is a collaborative text editor: everyone on a pad sees the text change as it's typed. The egg keeps pads in SQLite, with the admin pages behind the admin account.
startup: [ -n "${ADMIN_PASSWORD:-}" ] || unset ADMIN_PASSWORD; if [ "${UPDATE_CHECK}" = 1 ]; then export UPDATES_TIER=notify PRIVACY_UPDATE_CHECK=true; else export UPDATES_TIER=off PRIVACY_UPDATE_CHECK=false; fi; export NODE_ENV=production ETHERPAD_PRODUCTION=true PORT={{SERVER_PORT}}; exec node --require ./etherpad/src/node_modules/tsx/dist/cjs/index.cjs etherpad/src/node/server.ts --settings /home/container/settings.json --apikey /home/container/APIKEY.txt --credentials /home/container/credentials.json

config.startup: {"done": ["You can access your Etherpad instance at"]}

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Etherpad: downloads the release's Debian package for the chosen version
# from GitHub (checked against GitHub's checksum) and unpacks the app into
# etherpad/, which is replaced only once the new one is complete. Pads and
# plugins (var/: the SQLite database, installed_plugins.json), settings.json
# and APIKEY.txt are never touched.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server
work=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
rm -rf "$work" && mkdir -p "$work"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
rm -rf .raptor-new
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }
case "$(uname -m)" in
    x86_64) arch=amd64 ;;
    aarch64) arch=arm64 ;;
    *) fail "Etherpad has no build for this CPU ($(uname -m))." ;;
esac

want="${VERSION:-latest}"
tag=latest
if [ "$want" != latest ]; then tag="v${want#v}"; fi
tag=$(gh-release tag ether/etherpad "$tag") || fail "Etherpad has no version $want. Set Version to latest, or to a release such as 3.3.17, then reinstall."
version="${tag#v}"

if [ -f etherpad/src/package.json ] && [ "$(jq -r .version etherpad/src/package.json)" = "$version" ]; then
    echo "Etherpad $version is already installed."
else
    deb=$(gh-release assets ether/etherpad "$tag" | awk -v re="^etherpad_${version//./[.]}-[0-9]+_${arch}[.]deb$" '$1 ~ re { print $1; exit }')
    [ -n "$deb" ] || fail "Etherpad $version has no package for this CPU ($arch). Choose a newer version."
    echo "Downloading Etherpad $version"
    gh-release download ether/etherpad "$tag" "$deb" "$work/etherpad.deb"
    dpkg-deb -x "$work/etherpad.deb" "$work/pkg"
    [ -f "$work/pkg/opt/etherpad/src/node/server.ts" ] || fail "Etherpad's package didn't have the app where it should. Report this to Raptor."
    mv "$work/pkg/opt/etherpad" .raptor-new
    cp -f "$work/pkg/usr/share/etherpad/settings.json.dist" settings.json.template
    # Pads and plugins live in var/, outside the app, so updates keep them.
    rm -rf .raptor-new/var
    ln -s ../var .raptor-new/var
    rm -rf etherpad
    mv .raptor-new etherpad
fi
mkdir -p var
# The plugin list Etherpad keeps (as its package writes it); without it,
# Etherpad tries to rebuild it with pnpm, which the server doesn't have.
if [ ! -f var/installed_plugins.json ]; then
    jq -n --arg v "$version" '{plugins: [{name: "ep_etherpad-lite", version: $v}]}' > var/installed_plugins.json
fi

# A first settings.json from Etherpad's own template: pads in SQLite, the
# admin pages (/admin) behind the admin account, whose password comes from
# Admin password, no update checks unless Update check is on. The port is
# the server's, at every start.
if [ ! -f settings.json ]; then
    [ -f settings.json.template ] || fail "Etherpad's settings template is missing. Reinstall to fetch it again."
    # Etherpad's single sign-on clients get random secrets instead of the
    # template's placeholders (this egg signs in with a password, but the
    # placeholders would still be accepted).
    admin_secret=$(head -c 24 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -d '/+=')
    user_secret=$(head -c 24 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -d '/+=')
    sed -e 's|^  "port": 9001,|  "port": "${PORT:9001}",|' \
        -e 's|^  "dbType": "dirty",|  "dbType": "sqlite",|' \
        -e 's|^    "filename": "var/dirty.db"|    "filename": "/home/container/var/etherpad.db"|' \
        -e 's|"tier": "${UPDATES_TIER:notify}"|"tier": "${UPDATES_TIER:off}"|' \
        -e 's|"updateCheck": "${PRIVACY_UPDATE_CHECK:true}"|"updateCheck": "${PRIVACY_UPDATE_CHECK:false}"|' \
        -e 's|^  "authenticationMethod": "${AUTHENTICATION_METHOD:sso}",|  "authenticationMethod": "apikey",\n\n  /* The admin account (Admin password); no password, no account. */\n  "users": {\n    "admin": {\n      "password": "${ADMIN_PASSWORD:null}",\n      "is_admin": true\n    }\n  },|' \
        -e "s|\${ADMIN_SECRET:admin}|\${ADMIN_SECRET:$admin_secret}|" \
        -e "s|\${USER_SECRET:user}|\${USER_SECRET:$user_secret}|" \
        settings.json.template > settings.json.new
    for want in '"port": "${PORT:9001}"' '"dbType": "sqlite"' 'var/etherpad.db' '${UPDATES_TIER:off}' '${PRIVACY_UPDATE_CHECK:false}' '"authenticationMethod": "apikey"' '${ADMIN_PASSWORD:null}' "$admin_secret" "$user_secret"; do
        grep -qF "$want" settings.json.new || fail "Etherpad's settings template has changed shape, so settings.json couldn't be written. Report this to Raptor."
    done
    mv settings.json.new settings.json
    echo "Wrote a first settings.json (SQLite, admin account from Admin password)."
fi
echo "Installed Etherpad $version."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The Etherpad version to install, such as 3.3.17, or latest. Reinstall to change it.

variables.name: Admin password
variables.description: The password of the admin account, which signs in to /admin. Leave it empty to have no admin account.

variables.name: Update check
variables.description: Set it to 1 to let Etherpad check GitHub for new versions and show them on the admin pages.
